About George

High-performance thinking, made personal.

George Gauntlett BSc (Hons) MCSP is a Chartered Physiotherapist and founder of George Gauntlett Physio. He also works in professional sport as a Senior Physiotherapist with Bath Rugby.

Previously, George worked as a Performance Physiotherapist with athletes from GB Triathlon, swimming and tennis, as well as across a wide range of other high-performance environments. His clinical experience also includes working in the NHS.

Alongside his specialist work in sports performance, George provides detailed assessment, treatment and rehabilitation for acute and chronic musculoskeletal injuries—supporting people with goals ranging from comfortable everyday movement to a full return to competition.

Who George treats

At Church Street Practice, George treats patients over the age of 16 with new injuries, longstanding pain, reduced mobility, and rehabilitation needs before or after surgery.

Athlete-level experience for everyone

You do not need to be an athlete to benefit from detailed assessment, clear explanations and rehabilitation informed by high-performance environments.

How George can help

Care designed around the person—not just the injury.

George combines detailed clinical reasoning, appropriate hands-on treatment and progressive exercise to RESOLVE pain, REBUILD strength, movement, and confidence and RETURN you to what you love.

Conditions treated

Injury assessment

A detailed history and physical assessment to identify the likely cause of your symptoms and create the right plan for you.

Hands-on treatment

Manual therapy and soft-tissue massage to reduce pain, improve mobility and restore function, used alongside rehabilitation where appropriate.

Pre- and post-operative rehabilitation

Expert care before and after surgery to prepare you well, optimise recovery and support the best possible outcome.

Injury rehabilitation

Structured rehabilitation to rebuild mobility, strength and confidence, helping you return to the activities that matter to you.

MRI and X-ray referrals to Bath Clinic

Where clinically indicated following assessment, George can refer for private MRI and X-ray imaging through Bath Clinic, helping ensure the right investigation is used at the right time.

Not everyone needs imaging — assessment comes first.

The 3 R's

A simple framework for a purposeful recovery.

Your plan evolves as your symptoms, confidence and physical capacity change.

RESOLVE

Understand the problem.

Identify the likely root cause, create clarity around what is driving your symptoms and begin reducing the barriers to movement.

Assessment · explanation · treatment
REBUILD

Develop your capacity.

Rebuild strength, mobility, control and tolerance with a tailored plan that progresses from your current starting point.

Exercise · progression · confidence
RETURN

Prepare for what matters.

Bridge the gap between rehabilitation and the real demands of your sport, work, training, hobbies and everyday life.

Testing · exposure · lasting results

FAQs

Before your first appointment.

What should I bring or wear?

Wear clothing that allows the relevant area and movements to be assessed. Bring useful medical letters, scan reports or post-operative guidance, plus a list of relevant medication where appropriate.

What happens during the initial assessment?

The appointment includes time to understand your symptoms and goals, a physical assessment, a clear explanation of the likely problem and an agreed plan. Treatment or initial rehabilitation may begin where appropriate.

Is the clinic only for athletes?

No. George works with clients from all walks of life. Goals may include returning to work, walking, hobbies, gym training, sport, family life or everyday movement after surgery.

What is the cancellation policy?

Please give as much notice as possible if you need to move or cancel an appointment. Cancellations made with less than 48 hours’ notice, and missed appointments, will be invoiced at the full cost of the booked appointment.

What should I do if my symptoms feel urgent?

The website and email are not monitored as an emergency service. For severe or rapidly worsening symptoms, significant trauma, new neurological symptoms or other urgent concerns, seek appropriate urgent medical help.
